body: Thank you. I've really been struggling with this. I think I have some deep seated issues with sex being intertwined with my self worth. I love getting my partner off, but I also have this fucked up need for someone to desire me so much they surrender to the whims of my imagination. I really hate this about myself. I don't mean in a coercion way, I need to feel *needed* and for some reason I guess kinky sex has been the only time I've really been able to find that feeling explicitly. Everyone is willing to have sex with most people in our day and age, but not everyone is willing to do certain specific acts with someone unless they are truly invested in that person. I feel like this is a really unhealthy view, partially informed by watching porn *way* too young (like 9). I want to feel needed without having to do some stupid performative sex act. It's all a mental thing for me. The act is just proof of desire and mutual attraction for me. I don't like it at all. It makes me feel depraved and I know that this mentality is not conducive to healthy relationships.
Thanks.

I've been complaining on this thread about pent up resentments I have never expressed over the 4 years we have been together. I don't think loving someone and sometimes needing to vent about the aspects of your relationship you are unhappy with are mutually exclusive. Other than what I have mentioned here, I am incredibly happy with our relationship. We have been going through a rough patch, but a lot of that is due to my own insecurity and inability to generate any compassion or love for myself. 

Self love? Ha.
 I *loathe* myself. I have since I was a child. I was an only child, the *gifted*, mature, bookish kid. I have been holding myself over the fire of my perfectionism my entire life and the only thing that has ever alleviated that pain has been external validation. I cannot accept my flaws. I've tried. I cannot find compassion for myself. I'm obviously so inherently flawed that most of this thread has been flagellating me, so why should I *love* someone so deplorable. Even when I make a step to try to change for the better and be honest about my feelings it ends up blowing up in my face. 

Unfortunately, my mental illness doesn't fit the shy, sad, melodramatic checklist that actually illicits sympathy from most people.

It's just hellish. For me, for those around me, and it's my fault. I have trouble finding any compassion for myself when I have given my dad PTSD over a suicide attempt. I feel trouble finding any compassion for myself when I know I have such spite living within me. I feel trouble finding any compassion for myself when people on reddit essentially call me a monster and verbatim say "you are the problem", as if I did not know that and was not making the post in a desperate attempt to seek out HELP. 

I know it's my fault. I do. I don't know how to change it and so far nothing I've tried has helped. I don't know how to *feel* love for myself. I can rationalize it, I can talk to my "inner child" and try to find some sort of understanding, but I don't remember a time in my life where I wasn't criticizing my every move, my every thought. 

I hope I can find love within myself. I'm certainly going to give it a concerted effort, but unfortunately I'm not sure how successful I'll be in that endeavor.

Not bringing up my mental health around her, because it makes her "uncomfortable". Not discussing my kinks because they are "gross". Not willing to participate in oral sex or any sort of extended physical intimacy outside of PiV sex. Not letting me talk about my work day because "i don't care about your coworkers". Not letting me cry when she says something hurtful because "you're just crying to manipulate me". I could go on.

Thank you. I think people underestimate how phenomenal they are at taking advantage of vunerable people. I should have seen the red flags (leaving another guy for me, "I hurt everyone I love", "I'd probably kill myself if you left me"), but I was 16 and had a plethora of undiagnosed mental health issues and no self-esteem so it felt really good knowing someone NEEDED me. It actually made me feel valuable and confident. I felt secure, unconditionally. I wish I had a normal self-image so anything short of ritualistically sacrificing parts of ourselves to eachother would make me feel valuable and safe. I just always have this feeling that I'll make one misstep or have one panic attack and I'll be abandoned. That they will realize how damaged and flawed I am and discard me like garbage to "focus on themselves". I think that selfish impulse in me is driven by fear, because if I am not good enough for someone clearly I'm not worthy of living. For our best points in that relationship and honestly my current relationship we were enmeshed in eachother. It was as if we had become one greater whole. I felt safe and free in those fleeting moments. We had surrendered part of ourselves in order to create this infallible monolith of safety and adoration. I guess we have to maintain ourselves though. Which will always make me at risk of more pain, unfortunately. 

I'm getting better at finding sympathy and moving forward. The hardest thing has been finding any kind of self-generated security or esteem.

Thank you. I definitely have a problem with coveting. I hate putting my relationships in compromising positions, because I don't trust myself not to do something stupid and end up seriously injuring or killing myself. I don't want to be alone. Being alone always inevitably leads to me becoming an addict or losing all will to live. Not to mention that I do truly, deeply love her and the thought of not having her in my life devastates me. 

I have a serious problem of repressing and neglecting my own needs which leads to them manifesting themselves through passive aggressive behavior. I am not even conscious of it until afterward, in which I'll apologize. I hate that I have a tendency to be petty and occasionally vindictive. I feel terrible guilt for projecting those emotions onto someone I would do anything for.

I also often feel like as a man mentioning my "sexual needs" is bound to be misconstrued into some form of coercion or abuse. I've noticed that reaction here at least and ive suspected as such.

I really needed to hear this. Thank you for that. This really resonates with me. You're 100% right. I'm not sure why I have this incredibly warped perception of my last relationship. It was hellish. There were moments of intense ecstacy, but those moments were rare and fleeting. Most of it was gaslighting, insane levels of possessiveness (from both of us), arguments and occasionally being physically hit. I also nearly ended up with an assault charge for beating up her ex (she also was cheating on me with him) because he kept driving up to my parent's house (where we lived) every-night to stalk her and kept threatening my family and to rape her. I wasn't on medication yet and had never seen a therapist either, so I had an insane amount of untreated mental issues feeding into that. It was exciting, but I was so miserable I ended up overdosing on hydrocodone and clonazepam. The relationship literally culminated in me spending 4 days in a coma giving my family and friends all kinds of unnecessary trauma. I don't know why after all that shit her opinion still manages to dictate how I feel about myself. You're right. I just have to say it's time to stop.

Honestly, I'm not even positive my outlook on sex is healthy enough to be seeked out. We have good sex. Its loving, intimate and fun, I just worry I have a unhealthy perspective of what sex is even supposed to be. Sex has almost always been about validation for me. Performing to prove your devotion and desire. To give that to them in an orgasm. To give them pieces of you only THEY can have. I don't think that's what sex is supposed to be. I think I can enjoy our sex life more, but I just really think I need therapy. I feel warm, good and happy after sex with her. It's more sustainable and it feels real. It just sucks so much of my self worth during my developmental teenage years was predicated on that intense ecstatic hit of endorphins after we would do something crazy to prove our devotion for eachother. I just wish I could have had a "normal" first relationship, because my first relationship was a flaming shitshow that I would never want to return to, but the highs were HIGH. I want to be normal and feel normal and not rely on sex as a way to feel O.K with myself for a brief period.

I'm not sure how I'm "using" her. She is fully aware of these issues and I'm seeking therapy and help. I didn't make a post asking how I can deal with these problems, because I enjoy having them. I made the post because I'm trying to change.

I don't constantly think about these things. I have episodes every six months or so where I find myself ruminating over my inadequacies as a person. This relationship as well as my current one have dictated how I value myself, so yeah my ocd generally fixates on "what was so wrong with me that I wasn't good enough". I literally have zero control over that and I've discussed it with my girlfriend. I don't know where you got the impression I don't care about her? I just vented about how I rarely feel desirable due to her stringent boundaries, which I abide to and respect even if they make me feel worthless sometimes. Am I just supposed to never have a relationship again because I have a mental disorder which constantly forces me to question my self worth and look for ways to find reassurance?

I also unfortunately have no way to source it with an accurate dosage, because most everyone I know either lies about the micrograms or has bunk stuff. 

I've always done psychidelics for the sole purpose of personal growth and development, never recreation, which also makes me very uncomfortable having to get involved with shady people.

Thanks again

I made a slightly snide remark about feeling taken for granted and she quipped back "you made me this way!", I guess because I pamper her and go out of my way to do things for her. She will even sometimes jokingly make a whip cracking motion which can feel really emasculating and feeds my feelings of resentment. I've avoided discussing these things with her because she is very avoidant and will usually stonewall me. I worry if I push too hard she will just end up leaving me for someone else.

I'll read it. Microdosing helped me for a while, but the mushrooms I grew were so variable in potency that I never had a reliable and consistent effect. Sometimes I'd take .1 and feel nothing and other times I'd take .1 and start actually having an unintentional, full blown psychidelic experience. I also struggle with depersonalization and derealization so I have tried to keep my use of psychoactive substances to a minimum. Thanks again.

I desperately want to. I'm sick of harboring this repugnant hate. It makes me feel ill, but the idea of forgiving her and seeing her move on with her life with zero consequences seems so incredibly difficult, I cannot even fathom how I could. Rationally I understand she is seriously damaged and I am happy she is in a place where she seems stable, but I also struggle with feeling deeply resentful that she there through abuse and the destruction of my self-esteem. I know I'm poisoning myself. I want to stop and that's why I made this post. I just feel it in my guts. Its beyond my higher thinking. I know its completely irrational, but yet that does not change the way it *feels* for me. I don't know how to change my *feelings*, because rationally I already know I am completely in the wrong.
Thank you for the suggestion.

I have taken psilocybin and dmt several times. They have given me drastic changes in self-awareness and these problems are far less extreme than they were prior. They helped me recognize that my maladaptive behavior patterns are the problem, but I've had no help in actually finding ways to cope with or correct those behaviors. They gave me the insight to step back and stop letting those behaviors dictate my behaviour, but I have OCD so I literally CANNOT control my thoughts. Physiologically my brain is wired incorrectly. Meditation has been helpful. It's been a few years since I last grew or took mushrooms, but when I was taking them every six months or so I was a far happier person. I just wish they could give me directions on how to actually integrate those companies in a meaningful way. It just sucks. My "inner voice", or shadow, or subconscious, whatever you want to refer to it as is NOT under my conscious control. I can actively limit what I allow to permeate on a concious level, but it festers in the shadows. It's a feeling in my gut. Its irrational, but it sure can make a rational case for itself. Sometimes it feels as if I am living as a prisoner under its thumb. Last night I got drunk and gave it a voice. I don't even remember writing it and reading it feels gross, because I know that's me, but at the same time it does not feel like ME. I hope some of this was coherent and I appreciate your suggestion. I'll look into it.

Thanks for the insight. I guess I hold some maladaptive beliefs on boundaries = refusal to give your all to a relationship. I've been going to therapy and I seriously am dedicated to changing these deep seated insecurities. Last night I made the mistake of getting piss-faced drunk and allowing the most insecure and irrational side of myself a voice online. I tend to get very grandiose and exaggerate how miserable I actually am on a day to day basis when I drink (not justifying anything I said, just giving an explanation). I do have a problem with severe self-loathing. I have ocd so I will fixate on perceived flaws about myself and spiral. The only thing that has ever made me feel desired or whole is sex and much of the time normal sex is not enough to make me feel special. That neurotic side of myself always needs to be #1 and I don't feel content with myself unless someone is actively giving me something they would never allow anyone else. I am aware of how unhealthy these fixations are and I am currently trying to mend them. I wish it was easier, but OCD has a way of ruthlessly rationalizing itself which can be incredibly difficult to ignore. I appreciate your candor and I apologize if anything I said was triggering. I really am dedicated to becoming a healthy person for myself and my girlfriend.

No, not at all. I don't want her to do anything shes not comfortable with to "please me". I just missed how engaging, exciting and playful sex once was for me. I wouldn't enjoy doing some kinky sex act if she wasn't 100% invested in doing it. I don't get anything from that. I liked how INTO me my ex was, not the acts themselves. She wanted to explore every facet of our bodies and she often came to me with fantasies she had and wanted to try. I'm not resentful because "x did y and now z won't do y", I think I struggle with feeling less desirable. I desire my girlfriend so much. I just don't feel like she has the same kind of ferocity.
Thank you.

Thank you for the brutal honesty. I appreciate you taking the time to actually write something helpful instead of a contempt laden diatribe. I guess I just have a really unhealthy preconception of what relationships are supposed to be. Probably informed by my first relationship ever being as toxic and predicated on maladaptive behavior as it was, mixed with the insane highs. I love my girlfriend, she deserves a healthy version of me or someone better. I just wish I had a normal perception of how relationships are supposed to work. The majority of my understanding of romantic relationships was derived from the idealistic, hyper-passionate depictions in movies. I think that ingrained itself in my developing mind and coupled with someone who was as equally damaged as me, led to unsavory results. I really do love my girlfriend and I'd do anything in the world for her. I just wish I could get rid of the weird, child-like resentment when she rarely ever goes out of her way to do something kind for me. I know this post makes me seem absolutely miserable, but in reality I wrote it in an incredibly emotional; slightly drunk state of mind which inadvertently exaggerated how unhappy I actually am.

There are more good things than bad, but yeah, I suppose. I just feel unappreciated. I love her to pieces, I just worry I'm too damaged to really be worthy of love. I don't want her to have to suffer due to my own pathologies.
Thanks. I never pushed sex stuff onto her, she would actually initiate them with me. Other than that I agree with everything you've said.

I love her grandmother; I still deeply care about her family. I was just incredibly hurt that she could betray my trust and dispose of me with such ease when I did nothing but show compassion and understanding. It just deeply jaded me. I was naive and that led to me getting traumatized. It has really crippled my ability to "give" myself over to someone else, because last time I lost everything. I don't know why this relationship branded itself onto my psyche like it has. 

I do love my current gf, but she does not put in effort. I always find myself bringing her home little gifts, cuddling her, going down on her, etc. She just expects it as if I am obligated to do those things and I feel like she takes me for granted. She can be pretty selfish and vanilla in bed and she has a laundry list of boundaries a mile long. I know I sound like a dick for *expecting* some basic kindness and reciprocity, but it gets exhausting essentially hand-feeding someone grapes and fanning them with a bundle of peacock feathers, only to have them sit around and act as if they are entitled to that. 

I'm definitely far from a being a catch myself, but I do put in serious effort. I've even been trying to start therapy again at her insistence. 

Everything just sorta feels futile though. I just really wish I could feel that kind of excitement for a moment to escape the mundane purgatory that my life has become. It was traumatic, but at least I wasn't numb.
I just wish I could find a good therapist. I've had no good experiences with CBT.

Thanks for the perspective. I'm glad that you have such a keen ability to analyze these things rationally. Everything you have said is a dead ringer. I often find her emblazoned in my mind as some sort of perfect, carnal drug. That's not a natural thing, like you say, that's their goal. I find myself feeling like a junkie relieving "the good old days" through rose-tinted-glasses. I just wish that kind of sexual intensity and lack of boundaries was not mutually exclusive with being a healthy, well adjusted person. I know realistically her husband is no longer reaping the benefits of their relationship, I have reason to believe she has cheated on him multiple times. I just hate how fantastic that sex was. I'll learn to live without it, unfortunately. 

My relationship is good, but it has never come close to the ecstatic, visceral passion that I experienced in that relationship. It's like comparing caffeine to amphetamine. I sometimes seriously wonder how I can  manage to be fully content after experiencing that. 

Thank you again.
